source_text:
Τίς γὰρ ὅλως ἀνθρώπων ἠπίστατο, τί ποτ̓ ἐστὶ θεὸς πρὶν αὐτὸν ἐλθεῖν;
ἢ τοὺς κενοὺς καὶ ληρώδεις ἐκείνων λόγους ἀποδέχῃ τῶν ἀξιοπίστων φιλοσόφων, ὧν οἱ μέν τινες πῦρ ἔφασαν εἶναι τὸν θεὸν ʽοὗ μέλλουσι χωρήσειν αὐτοί, τοῦτο καλοῦσι θεόν̓, οἱ δὲ ὕδωρ, οἱ δ’ ἄλλο τι τῶν στοιχείων τῶν ἐκτισμένων ὑπὸ θεοῦ;
καίτοι γε, εἴ τις τούτων τῶν λόγων ἀποδεκτός ἐστι, δύναιτ̓ ἂν καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν κτισμάτων ἓν ἕκαστον ὁμοίως ἀποφαίνεσθαι θεόν.
ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν τερατεία καὶ πλάνη τῶν γοήτων ἐστίν:
ἀνθρώπων δὲ οὐδεὶς οὔτε εἶδεν οὔτε ἐγνώρισεν, αὐτὸς δὲ ἑαυτὸν ἐπέδειξεν.
ἐπέδειξε δὲ διὰ πίστεως, ᾗ μόνῃ θεὸν ἰδεῖν συγκεχώρηται.
ὁ γὰρ δεσπότης καὶ δημιουργὸς τῶν ὅλων θεός, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ πάντα καὶ κατὰ τάξιν διακρίνας, οὐ μόνον φιλάνθρωπος ἐγένετο, ἀλλὰ καὶ μακρόθυμος.
ἀλλ’ οὗτος ἦν μὲν ἀεὶ τοιοῦτος καὶ ἔστι καὶ ἔσται, χρηστὸς καὶ ἀγαθὸς καὶ ἀόργητος καὶ ἀληθής, καὶ μόνος ἀγαθός ἐστιν:
ἐννοήσας δὲ μεγάλην καὶ ἄφραστον ἔννοιαν ἀνεκοινώσατο μόνῳ τῷ παιδί.
ἐν ὅσῳ μὲν οὖν κατεῖχεν ἐν μυστηρίῳ καὶ διετήρει τὴν σοφὴν αὐτοῦ βουλήν, ἀμελεῖν ἡμῶν καὶ ἀφροντιστεῖν ἐδόκει:
ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀπεκάλυψε διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ παιδὸς καὶ ἐφανέρωσε τὰ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἡτοιμασμένα, πάνθ̓ ἅμα παρέσχεν ἡμῖν καὶ μετασχεῖν τῶν εὐεργεσιῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰδεῖν καὶ νοῆσαι, ἃ τίς ἂν πώποτε προσεδόκησεν ἡμῶν;
thought_title: God revealed himself through faith alone
orientation: The author is arguing that no human being could know God before the Son came, and that God revealed himself through faith.
pass_a_gloss: For who of human beings at all knew what God ever is before he came? Or do you accept the empty and foolish words of those philosophers, of the trustworthy ones, of whom some said fire to be God (to which they themselves are about to go, this they call God), others water, others another of the elements of the things created by God? And yet, if any of these words is acceptable, one could also declare each one of the remaining creatures similarly to be God. But these things are wonder-working and deceit of the charlatans. And of human beings no one either saw or knew, but he himself showed himself. And he showed through faith, by which alone it has been granted to see God. For the master and craftsman of all things, God, the one who made all things and distinguished them according to order, not only became loving toward humanity, but also long-suffering. But this one was always such and is and will be, kind and good and without anger and true, and alone is good. And having conceived a great and unutterable thought, he shared it with the Son alone. So while he held in mystery and kept his wise counsel, he seemed to neglect us and to be unconcerned. But when he revealed through the beloved child and made manifest the things prepared from the beginning, he provided all things at once to us, both to share in his benefits and to see and to understand, which things who of us would ever have expected?

choices.why: The noun denotes the performing of marvels or portents, fitting the charlatans' deceptive display; 'wonder-working' keeps the active, showy sense.
The term refers to deceivers who use tricks and false claims; 'charlatans' captures the fraudulent, performative character better than 'sorcerers,' which overemphasizes magic.

The compound means 'loving humans'; rendering it as a phrase preserves the literal sense of the Greek compound without importing a single English word like 'philanthropic' that sounds modern and institutional.
The alpha-privative adjective literally means 'not angry' or 'without wrath'; 'without anger' is the most direct literal rendering.
The middle verb means 'communicated' or 'imparted' to someone; 'shared it' is plain and keeps the sense of intimate disclosure to the child alone.
The glossary identifies παῖς as the Son; 'child' is the literal sense and matches the intimate father-child relation in this passage, while 'servant' would lose the filial meaning.

pass_b_english: Who among human beings had any idea at all what God is before he came? Or do you accept those empty and foolish arguments of the philosophers who are considered trustworthy? Some of them said that God is fire, and they call the very thing they are going to end up in God. Others said water, and others one or another of the elements that were created by God. And yet, if any of these arguments were acceptable, then each of the other created things could just as easily be declared God. But all this is the wonder-working and deceit of charlatans. No human being has ever seen God or known him, but he has shown himself. He has shown himself through faith, and through faith alone has it been granted to see God.

For God, the Master and Maker of all things, who made everything and set it in order, was not only loving toward humanity but also patient. He was always like this, and is, and will be: kind and good and without anger and true, and he alone is good. But when he conceived a great and unutterable thought, he shared it with his child alone. So as long as he kept his wise plan hidden in mystery and guarded it, he seemed to neglect us and take no thought for us. But when he revealed it through his beloved child and made known what had been prepared from the beginning, he gave us everything at once: to share in his benefits, and to see and understand things that none of us could ever have expected.

problems.quote: the truth and the holy and incomprehensible Word
problems.why: The Son/Christ is given many different titles across sections; a first-time reader may not realize they all refer to the same figure.
problems.fix: Add a note at first mention that 'the Word' is the Son of God, identified with Christ.

problems.quote: Some of them said that God is fire—they call the very thing they are going to end up in “God”
problems.why: The dash and quotation marks around 'God' make it unclear whether this is the author's aside or a quoted philosopher's claim.
problems.fix: Clarify that the author is paraphrasing philosopher views, not quoting directly.

edits.old: Some of them said that God is fire—they call the very thing they are going to end up in “God”—others said water, others one or another of the elements that were created by God.
edits.new: Some of them said that God is fire, calling the very thing they are going to end up in God; others said water, others one or another of the elements that were created by God.

fixed: The glossary problem about 'the Word' does not apply to this section, since the Word is not mentioned here.
The speaker problem was fixed by removing the dash and quotation marks, making it clear the author is paraphrasing the philosophers' views rather than quoting them directly.

problems.why: The same divine person is called “God”, “the Father”, and “the Almighty” in different sections, which may suggest distinct beings.
problems.fix: Standardise to one term, e.g., “God (the Father)”.

problems.quote: he shared it with his child alone
problems.why: 'child' vs 'Son' for same figure may confuse reader about identity.
problems.fix: Use 'Son' consistently for the divine figure.

edits.old: he shared it with his child alone
edits.new: he shared it with his Son alone

fixed: The glossary issue about 'what God they have trusted' is not a problem in the English text itself; the English consistently uses 'God' for the divine person, and the source does not use 'the Father' or 'the Almighty' in this section. No change needed.
Changed 'child' to 'Son' in both the English and the literal gloss to standardize the divine figure's identity.

polish.changed: Clarified the author's aside about philosophers calling fire God, removed the dash and quotation marks that obscured the speaker, and kept the flow natural for reading aloud.
